prop: The rendered section follows compose.rs's shipped conventions with one deliberate difference. A "## Transplants" section renders beside the modification-target section: per live transplant, the donor fact id with its extent labels (labels, never absolute keys — the committed-document rule), the destination target id and symbol, and one entry per live premise carrying the selected text verbatim in a fenced block with the discharging claim id beside it; withdrawn transplants and premises are dropped, and once any claim exists the section renders even when empty ("none declared"), because the hole is the finding — the same visibility answer to under-declaration the target section shipped. prop: The acknowledgement event cannot live in `prose.jsonl`. `ProseEvent` is an internally-tagged serde enum over exactly `Create` and `Revise`, and `workspace::read_jsonl` propagates any line's parse failure as an error over the whole log rather than skipping it; empirically, a build at this pin reading a `prose.jsonl` containing one valid `Create` line and one `{"event":"Ack",...}` line fails the entire read with `unknown variant \`Ack\`, expected \`Create\` or \`Revise\`` and exits 1. A new tag value therefore makes every older build unable to read even the prose it already understood.

prop: The acknowledgement log is re-homeable into TET-36's obligation ledger without rewriting a single event, because no field in it is specific to this residue. It records a block id, the block's text and citation list, a digest per cited claim, a reason and a timestamp; it records none of the quantities `prose_after_proof` derives — not the anchor, not any claim's first proof, not the block timestamp, not whether the block was listed. A general ledger consuming these as discharge records for one obligation class therefore needs the events as they stand and a rule that reads them, which is a re-homing rather than a rework.
